payload.headline: NVIDIA jumps 31% to 165.05 as Huang returns; wait moves to hold

summary.thesis: Huang's confirmed return removes the main governance shock, while the business data is unchanged and very strong: sales up 105.85% and operating margin at 65.21%. The open question is whether that margin can last.
summary.decision: Long-term the call moves from wait to hold, because the price is back above the level that yesterday's note said would end the breakdown. Swing is wait: the next resistance is close and the stop would sit far below.
summary.act_at: Hold while the price closes above 147.15; buy at 114.82

payload.happening: NVIDIA closed at 165.05, up 31.48% in one day, after the company's newsroom confirmed that the board reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director. Trump reportedly endorsed the return and said the US has no evidence of wrongdoing. US lawmakers reportedly vowed to sharpen their probes of Huang. Our data has no earnings date.
payload.business: Today's news changes governance and sentiment, not the business. The business numbers come from the quarter that ended 2026-07-26. In that quarter, sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, up from 73.21% two quarters before. Operating margin rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow (cash left after running the business and investing in it) reached 127.0B over the last twelve months, up from 72.0B. The company holds 23.2B more cash than debt, so its finances are not at risk. Two things in the filings are at risk. First, the 65% operating margin is at the top of its five-year range of 16–65%, and peaks like this usually fade. Second, money customers still owe the company rose 127% while quarterly sales rose 106%. That can mean sales were pulled into earlier quarters or customers are paying more slowly. The governance risk is smaller but not gone: lawmakers' probes reportedly continue, and insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set trading plans. Analysts have kept raising estimates. Next-year EPS (earnings per share) is 16.61, up from 13.0 ninety days ago.

worth.text: At 165.05, the stock trades at 20.8 times trailing earnings and 9.9 times next year's estimated earnings. Its price-to-sales ratio is 13.1, close to the peer median of 13.3, and at the very bottom (0th percentile) of NVIDIA's own five-year range. The cash-flow model (DCF, which values a company by its future cash) gives 191.49 in the bear case, 222.58 in the base case and 264.22 in the bull case. Valuing the stock at its usual price-to-sales ratio gives 217.35 to 411.04. Note that the data's valuation summary still quotes the old 2026-11-20 price of 125.53. Today's price implies that free cash flow starts growing at 22% a year. A 20% starting rate gives 152.77 and a 30% rate gives 222.58, so the market is pricing growth near the low end of what has happened recently. The gap between the methods mostly comes from two assumptions: how fast growth starts and whether the margin holds. If operating margin falls to 48%, the model value drops to 114.82. At 32%, it drops to 76.87. So the margin is the assumption that matters most.
worth.key_assumption: Operating margin stays near 65.21% instead of fading toward 48%, while free cash flow grows from 127.0B at a starting rate of about 20% or more.

bull: Growth is speeding up, not slowing: quarterly sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, up from 73.21% two quarters before.
Analysts keep raising forecasts: next-year EPS is 16.61, up 27.7% in 90 days, which puts the stock at only 9.9 times next year's earnings.
The cash-flow model's base value of 222.58 and even its bear value of 191.49 sit above today's 165.05, and the price implies only 22% starting growth.
bear: Operating margin of 65.21% is at the top of its five-year range of 16–65%. If it falls to 48%, the model value is 114.82, well below today's price.
Money owed by customers rose 127% while sales rose 106%, which may mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly.
The trend is still down: the price is below the falling 20-day average (178.91) and 50-day average (206.08), and heavy resistance sits at 174.23–180.81, a zone the price has touched 6 times.

levels.what: Bottom of the only support zone (147.15–150.45). A close below it would undo today's recovery and send the call back to wait.
The model value if operating margin falls to 48%. Buy at 114.82, because that price already allows for a large margin fade.
The base-case cash-flow value. Up to this level, the price only assumes the margin and growth the data already shows.

longterm.why: The automated rule says 'Buy now' and the committee says 'Hold'. Most of the upside to fair value depends on a margin that sits at a five-year peak, and the receivables and probe risks are still open, so hold rather than add.

swing.why: The price sits inside the 163.9–171.33 zone. Resistance starts at 174.23, less than one average daily range (ATR, 13.22) away. A sensible stop would go under 147.15, which is much farther. The risk is too large for the reward until the price pulls back into 147.15–150.45 or closes above 180.81.

decision.timing: There is no earnings date in our data. The next quarterly filing will show whether the margin and customer payments hold, and lawmakers' probes could move the price sooner. The options data predates today's jump (its underlying price is 125.53), so its expected move is out of date.

change_mind: A close below 147.15 would undo the recovery and send the long-term call back to wait.
If the next filing shows operating margin below 58.09%, or receivables again growing faster than sales, the margin assumption fails and the relevant value falls toward 114.82.
A close above 180.81 with next-year EPS estimates at or above 16.61 would clear the most-tested resistance zone and support moving from hold to add.
payload.what_changed: Changed: the long-term call moved from wait to hold because NVIDIA confirmed Huang's reinstatement and the price closed at 165.05, above the 150.14 level that yesterday's note set as the end of the breakdown.
